subject: Scientific American
hook: SCIENTIFIC AMERICAN IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Scientific American, the oldest continuously published magazine in the United States, was essentially rebooted in 1948 by three partners who purchased the brand but discarded everything else to launch a completely different magazine under the same name.
angle_support: In 1948, three partners who were planning on starting a new popular science magazine, to be called The Sciences, purchased the assets of the old Scientific American instead and put its name on the designs they had created for their new magazine.
Thus the partners—publisher Gerard Piel, editor Dennis Flanagan, and general manager Donald H. Miller Jr. essentially created a new magazine.
title: The 1948 Scientific American Reboot
description: While often cited as the oldest magazine in the US, the Scientific American we recognize today was essentially a new publication started by three partners in 1948, who repurposed the brand for a completely different editorial vision.
narration: SCIENTIFIC AMERICAN IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture a legacy publication that has evolved steadily since 1845. It was closer to a total reboot. Everything changed in 1948 when new owners took control. Three partners originally intended to launch a brand new magazine called The Sciences. Instead, they purchased the dying Scientific American, discarded its entire format, and slapped its historic name onto their own entirely different design project. The magazine you know today is actually a clever corporate disguise.
